clue.text: Audience joining in disrupted Nolans gig

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; the Nolans were an Irish girl group

explanation.surface: A concert by the Nolans sisters is interrupted when the crowd joins in.
explanation.definitionFit: A singalong is an occasion where the listeners sing along with the performers, so the crowd takes part.

clue.text: Investigate American saving schemes …

parts.note: to sus (or suss) out is to investigate
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone looks into American savings plans, the clue running on into the next one.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue to 2 down, which repeats 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: A susu is a West African and Caribbean savings club in which members pool regular contributions and take turns drawing the pot.

clue.text: … American arranged privately

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American schemes are set up quietly, out of public view.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole word American is the fodder; the dots carry on the story from 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a Latin legal phrase for proceedings held in private, with the public excluded.

clue.text: Traps with king in cards

indicators.note: traps with a letter in them hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone sets traps holding a king among the playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cards' looks like playing cards, but a card is also an odd or eccentric person; 'with ... in' places the king inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gink is slang for a fellow, especially an odd one, just as a card is a comic or eccentric character.

clue.text: Setting diet regime finally

parts.note: a lo-cal diet is low in calories

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of regime

explanation.surface: A slimmer's regime is being set up at last.
explanation.walkthrough: LO-CAL is short for low-calorie, a description of a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is the place or scene where something happens, the same sense as a setting.

clue.text: Sign of encouragement with company backing end for fat cat

indicators.note: backing in a down clue means running back up, so the letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cry of approval
CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: end for picks out the last letter of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of fat

explanation.surface: A firm cheers on its fat cat executive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat cat' reads as one phrase about a rich boss, but fat only supplies a letter and cat is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Old resident female about to give up — time to go?

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a gal is a girl or woman

indicators.note: time to go says the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: to remit is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: An elderly woman resident is about to move out, asking if it is time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female about to give up' reads as a woman on the point of quitting, but 'about' is the container signal and 'to give up' is a verb to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gremial is an obsolete word for a resident member of a society or university, one living within its bosom.

clue.text: Spooner's sin boiling smalls at Oxford?

indicators.note: something boiling is churned about, so its letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: Dr Spooner, the Oxford don, commits the sin of boiling his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner looks like a spoonerism signal, but his name is simply fodder. Smalls is British slang for underwear and also an Oxford nickname for this exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Responsions were the first examination at Oxford University, known colloquially as smalls, abolished in 1960.

clue.text: Tie-dyed blanket perhaps thrown over Przewalski's horse

indicators.note: a blanket thrown over is flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ikat is a fabric whose threads are tie-dyed before weaving

explanation.surface: A colourful tie-dyed blanket is draped over a wild Mongolian horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps' marks ikat as one example of a tie-dyed cloth that might make a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Taki (or takhi) is the Mongolian name for Przewalski's horse, the wild horse of the Asian steppes.

clue.text: Buries again unnamed veteran German soldiers

indicators.note: unnamed means with no name, so the letter standing for name is removed

parts.note: to reinter is to bury again

explanation.surface: Old German war veterans, nameless, are laid to rest a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name. 'Veteran' belongs to the definition: these soldiers are historical.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiters were German cavalry soldiers of the 16th and 17th centuries, now long past, hence veteran.

clue.text: Universal joint keeping end of piston square

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of piston
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A mechanic's universal joint holds the end of a piston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal joint' looks like one engineering part, but it splits into a letter and a body joint, with the piston's end inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone square is old-fashioned and conventional, the opposite of being fashionable or cool.

clue.text: American after spell flying claimed base where F-15 functions

indicators.note: after places the American piece behind the spell piece in the word

parts.note: a hex is a magic spell

indicators.note: flying letters scatter and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American pilot, after a spell flying, says where the F-15 fighter jets operate from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' and 'F-15' suggest an air force base, but in hexadecimal F stands for 15, so the base is a number base.
explanation.definitionFit: Hexadecimal is the base-16 number system, in which the digit F represents fifteen.

clue.text: Sheaths are fabricated in line for arrows

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the following piece

parts.note: the oche is the line a darts player stands behind; arrows is slang for darts

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters are constructed anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Quivers are made to hold arrows in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrows' suggests archery, but in pub language arrows are darts, and the oche is where you throw from.
explanation.definitionFit: An ochrea is a botanical sheath formed by stipules wrapping a plant's stem; the plural is ochreae.

clue.text: Striking century in chase

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to sic is to set upon or chase, as a dog is told to
cen. is an abbreviation for century

explanation.surface: A batsman scores a remarkable hundred during a run chase.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a century in a run chase hides a dictionary abbreviation and the verb sic, used to urge a dog on.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenery that is scenic is impressive to look at, so the word can stand for visually striking.

clue.text: Fine skin covers Arabic hand

indicators.note: the opening words cover, that is contain, the answer within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Delicate skin covers an Arab person's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is not a body part here but a style of handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Neskhi or neski is the cursive script in which Arabic is usually written and printed, a hand in the calligraphic sense.

clue.text: Fruit to serve that's past it — alternative to like it?

parts.note: ka is an obsolete Scots verb meaning to serve, as in 'ka me, ka thee'
the saying is 'like it or lump it', so lump it is the other choice

explanation.surface: Serving overripe fruit, a host tells guests they will have to put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's past it' sounds like stale fruit but marks the serving verb as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: The kalumpit is a Philippine tree and its edible olive-like fruit.

clue.text: Small potatoes? Yes and no

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
mash is mashed potato

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is a trifling matter, the answer is both yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: Smash is a British brand of instant mashed potato: potatoes, yes, but a dried powder, so also no.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand is made from dehydrated potato granules, so it both is and is not real potatoes.

clue.text: Love Bug bearing spot of oil, one on the wing

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to bug someone is to annoy or rile them

indicators.note: a spot of something is a small bit, here its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of oil

explanation.surface: Herbie, the Love Bug car, carries a spot of oil and a passenger on a wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love Bug' calls up the Disney Beetle car, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriole is a brightly coloured songbird, a creature that is often seen in flight.

clue.text: Aspiring plan about to eke out old, old remedy

indicators.note: about means going around, so the reversed plan wraps the next piece
aspiring here means rising upward, and in a down clue that reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: a model is a plan or design
ech is an old form of eche, meaning to eke out

explanation.surface: An ambitious scheme is about to stretch an elderly person's medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiring' looks like hopeful, but means climbing, which turns the plan upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Leechdom is an Old English word for a medicine or cure, from leech, an old name for a doctor.

clue.text: Casing of enamelled metals beaten for small gongs

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters are reworked
the casing of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of enamelled
taken as written

explanation.surface: Enamelled metal is hammered into small decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: Gong is British slang for a medal or decoration, not a percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A medalet is a small medal, and gongs is informal British slang for medals or honours.

clue.text: Stopped by sophomore's college dance

indicators.note: the answer is stopped, held fast, by the words that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A second-year student drops in to the college ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A sophomore is an American second-year student.
explanation.definitionFit: Moresco is an old name for the morris or Moorish dance, a variant of moresque.

clue.text: Alzheimer's treatment likely to include grain

indicators.note: to include means to take inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: apt to do something means likely to do it
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A dementia therapy will probably contain a cereal ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Aricept is the brand name of donepezil, a drug prescribed to ease the symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

clue.text: Edge aside from latest of Mr Bean's brainwaves

indicators.note: aside from means without, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: a rim is an edge

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of Mr
pulses are beans and other edible seeds; the 's makes it plural

explanation.surface: Mr Bean, the comic character, has sudden bright ideas on the edge of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bean is Rowan Atkinson's bumbling TV character, but here Mr and Bean split up: one gives a letter, the other a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden urge or inspired idea is an impulse, much as a brainwave is a sudden clever thought.

clue.text: Regularly impose triages, they decide our fate

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of each word

explanation.surface: Hospital staff routinely impose triage, deciding which patients live.
explanation.walkthrough: Triage, sorting patients by urgency, makes the life-and-death surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moerae (Moirai) were the three Fates of Greek myth, who spun, measured and cut the thread of each life.

clue.text: What's agreed prior to match, parking up to take in McDonald's run?

indicators.note: to take in means to hold inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
taken as written
ren is a Scots word for run; the Mc name signals Scotland

explanation.surface: Before a game, a driver parks and grabs a McDonald's meal on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'McDonald's' looks like the burger chain but just marks the word as Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenup is a prenuptial agreement, signed before a wedding; match here means marriage.

clue.text: Here you see eg steeplechasing, losing a grand, ending up with nothing?

indicators.note: ending up with puts the last piece at the tail of the word
losing means giving something up, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: steeplechasing is a kind of horse racing
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A punter at the races loses a thousand and ends up with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The gambling story fits the answer neatly: the definition and the losses both belong at a track with a casino.
explanation.definitionFit: A racino is a racetrack combined with a casino, so horse racing such as steeplechasing is seen there.

clue.text: Principles of poker lie in considering a fold

indicators.note: principles are first things, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A poker player's principles say that bluffing is the way to decide whether to fold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' looks like the poker action of quitting a hand, but it is the definition in its anatomical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plica is a fold of skin or membrane in anatomy, from the Latin for a fold.

clue.text: Recipe in list to discover

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a ship that lists leans to one side
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on a prescription

explanation.surface: Someone checks a list of recipes to find something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb used of a tilting ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to find out about it, which is one sense of discover.

clue.text: Abandoned wife? One trifles largely on the rebound

indicators.note: something on the rebound bounces back, so the letters run in the other direction
largely means most but not all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a means one
nugae is the Latin word for trifles, used in English too

explanation.surface: A woman left by her husband trifles with a new man on the rebound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rebound' is a nice touch: it is both the reversal and what a deserted spouse might be.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish law an aguna is a woman whose husband has left or vanished without granting a divorce, so she cannot remarry.

clue.text: Those expelled left out of selective broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
out of means removed from, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: The people kicked out were left out of a programme that was choosy about its guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the L from selective leaves the eight letters that are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Evictees are people evicted, expelled from a home or property by legal process.

clue.text: Mediaeval court versus His Majesty accepts closure of defence

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for versus
HM is the abbreviation for His Majesty

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of defence

explanation.surface: In an old court case, the Crown takes on the defence until the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vehm was a secret tribunal system of medieval Westphalia, the Vehmgericht, that tried crimes in Germany.

clue.text: Scattered seed shifting 90 degrees at the end

indicators.note: a quarter turn moves one compass point to the next, so the final letter changes to its neighbouring direction

parts.note: semen is seed

explanation.surface: Seed is strewn about as a sower swings round a quarter turn at the end of a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The final N, for north, turns 90 degrees clockwise to E, for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Semé (semee) is a heraldic term for a field scattered or powdered with small charges.

clue.text: Rhea let go holding head right back

indicators.note: head right back sends the opening letter all the way to the end

parts.note: to unhand someone is to let go of them

explanation.surface: Someone releases a large bird while holding its head right back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' looks like part of the grip, but it links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The nhandu is the South American rhea, a large flightless bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Fellow scraping off piece of gateau's nut topping

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: scraping off means removing, so part of the next word is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
piece and gat are both slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A man scrapes the nut topping off a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of gateau' looks like a slice, but piece is gun slang; nut is slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapeau is a hat, the covering that sits on top of one's nut, or head.

clue.text: Porcupine ruffling short snout round tail of another

indicators.note: round means going around, so the mixed letters surround another piece
ruffling disturbs and disorders, so the letters are mixed
short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of another

explanation.surface: A porcupine ruffles its quills around another animal's short snout.
explanation.definitionFit: The urson is the Canadian or North American tree porcupine.

clue.text: Bacterium found in orifice after eating maize cake

indicators.note: eating means swallowing, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a trema is an orifice or opening, a sense found in Chambers
pone is American corn bread made from maize

explanation.surface: A germ turns up in someone's mouth after they eat corn bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Treponema is a genus of spiral bacteria, one species of which causes syphilis.
